name: LME49713 (National / TI high-fidelity current-feedback audio op-amp)
tagline: National's current-feedback single: 1.9 nV/√Hz, 0.00036% THD+N, 1900 V/µs, ±100 mA. Head-Fi and diyAudio builders praise it for quiet headphone and buffer stages with strong drive.
technology: Single-channel bipolar current-feedback (CFB) audio op-amp from National's LME49xxx high-performance audio line. Someone who worked on the chip said it was made on National's LME high-voltage process (forum attribution). Packages: SOIC-8 and 8-lead TO-99 metal can; no DIP-8. Supply ±5 V to ±18 V.

part_numbers.notes: Generic device name. Single current-feedback op-amp. TI literature SNAS386.
8-lead TO-99 metal can, lead-free orderable. Digi-Key 296-41515-ND. LCSC and broker stock still listed.
TO-99 metal can base marking/ordering code (National era, before /NOPB).
SOIC-8 in rails, lead-free. Digi-Key lists LME49713MAX/NOPB as the alternate packaging.

lineage.notes: Part of the LME49xxx high-performance audio op-amp family, alongside LME49710/LME49720/LME49740. The TI datasheet header gives the original release as September 2007. National-format revisions dated May 21, 2010 and June 2, 2010 survive on mirrors.

lineage.role: Owner after acquiring National (September 2011); discontinued the part
lineage.notes: Reissued the datasheet as SNAS386F in March 2013. Distributors list the part as obsolete, with the last-time buy expiring 2017-11-02. No TI discontinuance notice (PDN) number was found.

typ, 1 kHz (load and level per datasheet)
typ small-signal. This is a current-feedback part, so bandwidth depends mostly on the feedback resistor rather than being a gain-bandwidth product.

reputation.summary: Head-Fi has a thread titled 'LME49713, could be a killer opamp'. On diyAudio, someone who worked on the chip called it the best-sounding op-amp made on National's LME high-voltage process, and said that in extended listening sessions it was preferred over voltage-feedback parts in most applications. One Head-Fi user called a simple headphone amp built with it 'quite amazing - dead silent and with real drive' and said it drives 150-ohm loads easily. It is a niche, enthusiast-praised part rather than a mainstream standard. It is not a drop-in replacement for standard duals, and it is fast and tricky to stabilise.
sonic_descriptors: real drive / effortless load driving (one Head-Fi user)
typical_uses: Headphone amplifier / output buffer (drives 150 Ω loads)
DAC output / I/V stages (on SOIC-to-DIP adapters)
Make-up gain stage for passive summing mixers (Gearspace RMS Folcrom thread)
caveats: Single channel, SOIC-8 or TO-99 only: needs an adapter for DIP-8 sockets and cannot directly replace dual NE5532/LME49720 parts.
Current-feedback part: the feedback resistor sets bandwidth and stability, and a capacitor must not go across the feedback resistor. Voltage-feedback circuits can oscillate.
diyAudio report: it ran very hot/oscillated in the NE5534 sockets of a Sony CDP-557ESD, where an AD844 worked instead.
Input bias current of about 1.8 µA typ can cause large offsets with high-value bias resistors.
Obsolete since the 2017 last-time buy, so sourcing is limited to old stock and brokers.

revision_history.changes: Initial release. Date taken from the TI header 'SEPTEMBER 2007'.
National-format update (Farnell copy). Change list not captured.
Last National-format revision (Octopart copy). Change list not captured.

TI-format reissue, header 'SNAS386F – SEPTEMBER 2007 – REVISED MARCH 2013'. The exact change list was not captured; for other 2013 ex-National reissues TI typically noted 'changed layout of National data sheet to TI format' (unconfirmed for this part).

counterfeit_notes: No LME49713-specific counterfeit reports were found. Fakes of its siblings (LME49720, LM4562) are well documented on diyAudio. The part has been obsolete since the 2017 last-time buy, and SOIC and TO-99 units on eBay, AliExpress or broker sites carry elevated remark/fake risk. Check marking, date code and the metal-can finish, and bench-test bias current, slew rate and distortion.
alternatives: AD844 (Analog Devices current-feedback, DIP-8 available; one diyAudio user found it stable where LME49713 oscillated)
LME49710 (National/TI voltage-feedback single from the same family; easier to stabilise; status not verified)
THS3091 / THS3491 (TI high-voltage current-feedback amplifiers; not audio-specified)
open_questions: How do TI revision letters A-E map to the National dated versions (Sept 2007 initial, May 21 2010, June 2 2010, and any 2008-2009 revisions)? Is June 2, 2010 really SNAS386E?

TI's own status for the part (Obsolete or NRND) and the discontinuance notice (PDN) number were not seen. Distributors show obsolete with last-time buy 2017-11-02.
No die change, PCN or 'same part number, different silicon' event was found. This is presumably because the part was discontinued rather than moved to a new process. Unconfirmed.

Status changed from 'unknown' to obsolete. Distributors list LME49713HA/NOPB as obsolete with last-time buy 2017-11-02, and LME49713MA/NOPB as obsolete with MAX/NOPB as the alternate packaging.
Added the orderable codes LME49713HA/NOPB, LME49713MA/NOPB and LME49713MAX/NOPB. Package mapping: HA = TO-99 metal can, MA = SOIC-8. One search summary wrongly called MA a TO-99 part.

claims_confirmed: The TI datasheet is SNAS386F, 'SEPTEMBER 2007–REVISED MARCH 2013' (https://media.digikey.com/pdf/Data%20Sheets/Texas%20Instruments%20PDFs/LME49713.pdf; https://www.mouser.com/ds/2/282/lme49713-224065.pdf).
The Farnell copy is the National-format datasheet dated May 21, 2010 (https://www.farnell.com/datasheets/577866.pdf).
The Octopart copy is the National-format datasheet for LME49713HA dated June 2, 2010 (https://datasheet.octopart.com/LME49713HA-National-Semiconductor-datasheet-15941891.pdf).
Supply ±5 V to ±18 V, noise 1.9 nV/√Hz, THD+N 0.00036% (https://media.digikey.com/pdf/Data%20Sheets/Texas%20Instruments%20PDFs/LME49713.pdf).
Slew rate ±1900 V/µs, output current ±100 mA, bandwidth 132 MHz, and closed-loop bandwidth set by the feedback resistor (https://www.farnell.com/datasheets/577866.pdf).
LME49713HA/NOPB is obsolete with last-time buy expiring 2017-11-02 (https://www.digikey.com/en/products/detail/texas-instruments/LME49713HA-NOPB/1997968; https://www.findchips.com/search/lme49713).
LME49713MA/NOPB is listed as obsolete, with LME49713MAX/NOPB as the alternate packaging (https://www.digikey.com/en/products/detail/texas-instruments/LME49713MA-NOPB/1836036).
The Head-Fi thread 'LME49713, could be a killer opamp' exists (https://www.head-fi.org/threads/lme49713-could-be-a-killer-opamp.267524/).

A diyAudio user reported the part running hot/oscillating in the NE5534 sockets of a Sony CDP-557ESD, where an AD844 worked instead (https://www.diyaudio.com/community/threads/lme49713-opamp-problem.151403/).

Forum posts say it is SO-8 single only, so NE5532 DIP sockets need adapters, and that a capacitor must not go across the feedback resistor (https://www.diyaudio.com/forums/analog-line-level/330762-lme49713.html).
